reason: A document whose statement times (an activity's start and end, a generation time and a usage time) are a `datetime.datetime` subclass whose isoformat gives nine fractional digits reads back from every format with those times cut to microseconds, and its attribute value ex:t reads back from the four text formats as a nine-digit xsd:dateTime `Literal`. The readers reject a statement time with more than six digits (#514), so the writers pass each statement time to `_xsd_datetime_text` with statement=True, from `ProvRecord._provn_formal_items`, `encode_json_container`, `encode_jsonld_statement` and `_encode_attribute_value`. With the earlier `_xsd_datetime_text` and its four callers restored, and again with `_xsd_datetime_text` writing every value through `datetime.isoformat` unbound, the whole suite fails only this test's json, xml, jsonld and provn rows.

An entity attribute `ex:t` given a `datetime` with +14:30 raises `ProvValueError` with the message `ex:t 2012-01-01T00:00:00+14:30 has a timezone offset beyond ±14:00`. #513 and `docs/reference/values.md`: a `datetime` with an offset beyond ±14:00 is an error.

In every format a document holding a `Literal` of an `xsd:dateTime` with +15:00 reads back equal and raises no `ProvWarning`. #513 and #522: a text outside the lexical space stays a `Literal` in every reader. `docs/reference/conformance.md` values table.

In the four text formats a document holding an `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` with a seven-digit fraction reads back equal and raises no `ProvWarning`. #514 and `docs/reference/conformance.md` values table: a typed literal with a fraction of more than six digits stays a `Literal`.

In the four text formats a start time with a seven-digit fraction raises the format's reader error. #514: a fraction beyond six digits is rejected as a time of a statement. `docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md`.

In every format a time written with +15:00 raises the format's reader error, chained to a `ProvValueError` with the exact message, with the reader's position text first, and not itself a `ValueError`. #513, and #653 for the reader error hierarchy.
`ProvDocument.activity` given `startTime="2011-11-16T24:00:00"` reads back as 2011-11-17 midnight. #237: the hour-24 form of xsd:dateTime reads as the next midnight.
`ProvDocument.activity` given `startTime="not a date"` raises `ProvException`. #237: a factory time parameter leaked a raw parser error instead of the library's `ProvException`.

`parse_xsd_datetime` returns the expected `datetime` for a Z, a naive, an offset and a one- to four-digit fraction text, and maps the hour-24 end-of-day form to midnight of the next day, with or without an offset. #237 (the hour-24 form), #514 (up to six fraction digits; the rows hold one to four) and XSD 1.1 section 3.3.7 as the `parse_xsd_datetime` docstring states it.

`parse_xsd_datetime` returns `None` for text outside the xsd:dateTime lexical form, for an hour-24 form with minutes, for an hour-24 rollover past year 9999 and for a fraction of seven or more digits. #514 and #237, and the `parse_xsd_datetime` docstring: accept the xsd:dateTime lexical space "and nothing else".

Reading Turtle with `prov:startedAtTime "2012-13-01T00:00:00"^^xsd:dateTime` raises `ProvRDFException` naming the subject, with a `ProvException` as its cause. #653: a reader raises its format error and chains the model's error. #522 and #515 for the time input.

Reading PROV-O with a seven-digit fraction gives a start time truncated to microseconds, and a typed attribute value reads as the truncated `datetime`. Caveat C10 and the values table of `docs/reference/conformance.md`, and #514.

`ProvDocument.activity` raises `ProvException` matching `Invalid value for attribute prov:startTime` for an `xsd:dateTime` literal with a month 13, an `xsd:string` literal with a valid date text and a language-tagged literal. #515 and `docs/reference/values.md`: only an `xsd:string` or `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` with a valid text is a time.

`activity` and `wasGeneratedBy` accept an `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` for `startTime`, `endTime` and `time`, and read back the `datetime`. #515: a `Literal` typed `xsd:dateTime` is a valid value for `prov:time`, `prov:startTime` and `prov:endTime`.

`ProvDocument.activity` raises `ProvValueError` for a start time beyond ±14:00 given as a string with +15:00, a string with -14:01, a `datetime` with +14:30 and an `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` with +15:00. #513 and XSD 1.1 section 3.3.7: no xsd:dateTime has an offset beyond ±14:00. `docs/reference/values.md` and `docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md`.

`ProvDocument.activity` raises no error or warning for start times with +14:00, -14:00, Z and no offset. #513 and the rule beside it, `test_time_beyond_the_offset_bound_raises`: the bound is ±14:00 inclusive and a naive time has no offset to check.

An entity attribute given `Literal("2011-11-16T16:05:33+15:00", XSD_DATETIME)` stays that `Literal` and raises no warning. #513 and `docs/reference/conformance.md` values table: a typed literal with an offset beyond ±14:00 stays a `Literal`.

An entity attribute given an `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` with +14:00, -14:00, Z or no offset is stored as the parsed `datetime`, with no warning. `docs/reference/values.md`: an `xsd:dateTime` `Literal` with a valid text is stored as a `datetime`. #513 for the bound.
